In this exercise you will practise choosing a plot type based on the question and the variable types.

Main job: **choose the geom that answers the question best**.

By the end, you should be able to choose a plot for:

- one continuous variable,
- two continuous variables,
- one continuous variable split by a group.

## Load packages and data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
blomkvist <- read_csv("data/blomkvist.csv")
blomkvist <- drop_na(blomkvist, smoker, rt_hand_d, rt_hand_nd, age)
```

```{r}
glimpse(blomkvist)
```

## Data structure and geoms

Different geoms expect different variables to be available in the data frame. Before choosing a geom, check whether the data have the columns needed for the visual comparison.

| Geom | Data structure it needs | Typical mapping |
|---|---|---|
| `geom_histogram()` | one row per observation and one numeric variable | `aes(x = numeric_variable)` |
| `geom_point()` | one row per observation and two numeric variables | `aes(x = numeric_variable_1, y = numeric_variable_2)` |
| colour or shape groups | a grouping variable in the same data frame | `aes(colour = group_variable)` |

<p class="take-home">The plot can only show variables that are present in the right structure for the geom.</p>

## Question 1: What is the distribution of age?

Age is one continuous variable, so a histogram is a good first choice. The data structure is simple: `age` is one numeric column, and each row is one participant.

Complete the plot.

```{r}
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = ___)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = ___, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)",
       y = "Number of participants") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Try two different `binwidth` values. What changes?

Write one sentence here: ___

### Choose a geom for the same question

Run both plots, then answer the question below the code chunk.

```{r}
# Option A: histogram
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  theme_minimal()

# Option B: scatterplot against participant id
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = id, y = age)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal()

```

Which plot better shows the distribution of age: the histogram or the scatterplot? Explain what makes the distribution easier to see.

Write your choice and reason here: ___

## Question 3: Are two reaction-time measures related?

Two continuous variables are often shown with a scatterplot. This works because `rt_hand_d` and `rt_hand_nd` are two numeric columns in the same row for each participant.

Complete the plot using dominant-hand reaction time on the x-axis and non-dominant-hand reaction time on the y-axis.

```{r}
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = ___, y = ___)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Dominant-hand reaction time (ms)",
       y = "Non-dominant-hand reaction time (ms)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

What should the viewer compare in this plot?

Write one sentence here: ___

### Choose a geom for the relationship question

Run both plots, then answer the question below the code chunk.

```{r}
# Option A: scatterplot
ggplot(data = blomkvist,
       mapping = aes(x = rt_hand_d, y = rt_hand_nd)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  theme_minimal()

# Option B: two separate histograms
ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = rt_hand_d)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 50, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data = blomkvist, mapping = aes(x = rt_hand_nd)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 50, fill = "grey70", colour = "white") +
  theme_minimal()

```

Which option better shows whether the two reaction-time measures are related: the scatterplot or the separate histograms? Explain what information is needed to see the relationship.

Write your choice and reason here: ___

## Question 4: Does the relationship differ by group?

Add `smoker` as a colour aesthetic. This works because the grouping variable is in the same data frame as the two reaction-time variables. Keep the rest of the plot simple.

```{r}
ggplot(data = blomkvist,
       mapping = aes(x = rt_hand_d, y = rt_hand_nd, colour = ___)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Dominant-hand reaction time (ms)",
       y = "Non-dominant-hand reaction time (ms)",
       colour = "Smoking status") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Does the colour mapping help the comparison, or does it make the plot harder to read?
